cells.tense: The distinction is being made now, careful and private, with the pen still in hand.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Name the build you are already inside and do today's part of it. Only today's. Stop when that part is done.
cells.core:
You can tell what deserves your attention from what only makes noise, and you do it without an audience. Distinguishing one thing from another is a practice, not a mood. Piece by piece it gets sorted until the real one stands clear, and staying with that work is how anything you steer by becomes visible at all.

A small portion is the whole method. A scale played until the finger knows the note, a paragraph cut to size, one joint fitted true. Give today's part today's size and let finishing be enough for the hour. You are already spending your attention well; the way to keep spending it is to stop once the part is done. The build goes on tomorrow, at the same size.

cells.tense: The distinction is being pressed toward a future it has not reached yet.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: Take the next bit of the work to whoever it serves and do it where they can see it. Skip the speech, keep the piece.
cells.core:
You can make sharp, careful distinctions, and when the edge gets pressed too hard it turns on tomorrow before today has landed. The fine work starts arriving before the thing it is sorting, and the quiet hours turn into bracing — the future prepared for before anyone asked. Nothing is broken. The pace is just ahead of where the work actually is.

Let one piece out where you can be watched, and skip the explanation. Wherever this has been done unseen, do the next part of it in front of the one it serves. Seen at its true size, the work releases instead of tightening. That is the whole move.

cells.tense: The door was left behind, but the person is still standing at it.
cells.act: accept what is offered for what you gave
cells.ask: Take what is handed to you for work already done — at full size, no trading it down.
cells.core:
The careful distinguishing that used to place things has gone quiet. You know what a thing is worth; you have stopped acting as if that matters. The scrutiny points at what is gone, or nowhere, and the exactness that settled a question no longer settles it. Trying harder will not bring it back — trying is what thinned it. What fills it comes from somewhere else.

Take what is handed to you for work already done. Not the discount version, not the polite refusal. Full size, both directions, one exchange. That is how the eye recovers its footing — by noticing what actually comes back when somebody is asked to meet what you made. Receiving is the practice.

cells.tense: The pen is moving, but the writer has not signed the page.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Sit with a vision of yours that has already landed somewhere — an hour inside it, nothing improved.
cells.core:
The fine sorting runs and runs, and the person doing it seldom gets written down. The eye goes to the work, or to what the work is for, and the one making the call stands off somewhere else. The practice is steady. The hand on the pen is unclaimed.

Underneath all that is a simpler form of the same thing, and it is worth going back to. A vision you built toward has arrived in some form — maybe not the full one, but here. Sit with something you imagined that is already real, for an hour, and take it exactly as it stands. Not as a stage toward what comes after. The one who thought it up gets credited by being there when the thing lands. That is the whole return.
